I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt to download the source pages failed because of a bug in my own code, and the tool then stopped me from making any more requests in this session. I never read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse notes from memory. They would have no real sources behind them, and any URLs I added would be guesses.

**What to do next:** ask me again in a new message and I'll start the research from scratch. I plan to read these pages first:
- Enduring Word: enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-32/
- Precept Austin: preceptaustin.org/psalm-32-commentary
- Bible Hub: the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages for Psalm 32
- NET Bible notes: netbible.org

Then I'll search for:
- **Protestant differences:** Reformed, Lutheran, Wesleyan and Baptist readings of verses 1–2 and 5, which deal with forgiveness, sins being "covered" and God not counting sin against someone. Paul quotes verses 1–2 in Romans 4.
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** Psalm 32 is one of the seven Penitential Psalms.
- **Hyper-grace teaching:** any treatment of confession in verse 5.

If you'd like, you can also say which verses or traditions matter most to you, so I can do those first if the tool limits me again.
